status_definitions.STILL_HOLDS: 新证据没有推翻原结论，且其边界仍可辩护。
status_definitions.STRENGTHENED: 新增独立证据提高了结论可信度或扩展了适用范围。
status_definitions.CONTESTED: 存在合理的理论、方法或实证冲突。
status_definitions.PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED: 已有工作直接回答部分问题，但核心机制或范围仍开放。
status_definitions.NO_LONGER_CLAIMABLE: 旧表述已被明确反例或领域进展削弱，不能继续作为 novelty claim。
status_definitions.NEW_CORE: 新增证据使某一问题成为研究主线的核心，而非边缘 future work。

claims.statement: Pictorial meaning 既受 visual resemblance 约束，也会随 shared interaction history 形成 interaction-specific conventions。
claims.boundary: Controlled single-category human drawing；yoked-vs-shuffled isolates same-producer sequence exposure, not mutual common ground or embodied AI.

claims.statement: Human–robot repeated reference interaction 可以出现稳定的 task-specific referring conventions，但现有 AI/LVLM grounding 仍不呈现完整的 human-like interactive adaptation。
claims.boundary: Human–robot and machine-adaptation studies use different roles/tasks; E3 is one-sided adaptive listening and does not establish reciprocal embodied convention.

claims.statement: 不能再笼统声称 situated AI communication 很少使用 interaction history 或 accumulated common ground。
claims.boundary: history-conditioned memory 不等于 mutual belief 或 shared convention；失效的是旧 gap wording，不是整个研究方向。

claims.statement: Personalization、shared memory 与 convention formation 必须保持概念区分。
claims.boundary: 现有工作尚未通过 causal comparison 证明 personalization-only 与 convention-aware mechanisms 的差异。

claims.statement: Human–robot emergent convention 已有直接研究，但开放式、跨模态、长期且双方可协商的 embodied convention 仍未被这些证据解决。
claims.boundary: C8 now provides full-text human–human physical multimodal evidence, but not human–AI reciprocity, counterfactual history, repair or transfer.

claims.statement: Convention lifecycle——formation、detection、repair、retention、forgetting 与 transfer——应成为 AMSC 的核心研究问题。
claims.boundary: 这是 agent synthesis / research opportunity，不是任何单篇论文的原始结论。

claims.statement: Human repeated reference 通过 presentation、positive evidence、repair 与 partner-specific history 建立 grounding；仅有表达缩短或 alignment 并不足以证明 convention。
claims.boundary: 证据来自 spoken laboratory human–human tasks；没有直接的 embodied-AI evidence。

claims.statement: 受控的 human physical collaboration 可形成可复用的 speech / gesture abstractions，并出现 dyad 之间分化的 multimodal strategies。
claims.boundary: 20 dyads、固定角色、4 次重复；没有 Agent 或 history-severed control。

claims.statement: Robot motion / gaze 可以同时承载 instrumental 与 relational meaning，因此不能再把 social 与 functional communication 写成清晰分离的两个领域。
claims.boundary: 证据主要来自 fixed designer-authored behavior 与 narrative / design synthesis；没有 history-dependent joint grounding。

claims.statement: Task-strategy adaptation、semantic partner adaptation 与 mutual convention 必须分别建模与测量。
claims.boundary: E2 测量 video / UI strategy switching；E3 是 one-sided reference adaptation。二者都没有建立 reciprocal embodied convention。

claims.statement: Same-producer exposure、style familiarity、task learning 与 mutually grounded convention 在现有证据中仍缺少充分的因果区分。
claims.boundary: 这是 Agent synthesis；C5/C6 属于同一 evidence lineage，success、shortening 或 alignment 都不是充分证据。

claims.statement: Signal form 本身不足以决定 meaning；local context、task discriminability、relationship 与 interaction history 会共同改变解释与表达成本。
claims.boundary: 证据来自不同媒介与任务，不能被合并成单一 causal mechanism，也不是 embodied human–AI convention evidence。

claims.statement: Robot gaze、motion、speech、LED 与 AR 已能表达 attention、intent、uncertainty、capability 与 repair options；真正开放的是 calibration、history-dependent grounding 与 partner-specific adaptation。
claims.boundary: 多数证据来自 designer-authored mappings 与短期受控任务；不能证明共同形成的 convention。

claims.statement: Long-term robot meaning 与 use 会在 routine、roles、maintenance、organizational practice、appropriation 与 developer feedback 中共同生成；culture 不能被缩减为静态国别 preference。
claims.boundary: 证据包括 theory、research agenda、小规模 field cases 与一篇摘要级论文；不证明 autonomous robot learning 或 partner-specific convention。

gaps.statement: 互动反馈与 shared history 如何改变 embodied signal 的 partner-specific meaning，以及 Agent 如何检测这种 meaning change。
gaps.research_implication: 研究重点应是 meaning formation mechanism，而不是再做单一 cue 是否有效的问卷比较。

gaps.statement: Human–embodied-AI dyads 如何形成、确认、修复并适当迁移对 shared interaction history 有因果依赖的 multimodal conventions。
gaps.research_implication: X17/X19 已封死广义 AI code-emergence novelty；新研究必须区分 alignment、audience design、attunement、memory 与真正的 partner-specific mutual convention。

gaps.statement: Convention lifecycle 的若干环节已有证据，但 reciprocal repair、retirement、partner/context transfer 与 shared-history counterfactual test 仍然开放。
gaps.research_implication: 应分阶段建立 lifecycle evidence：先检验 shared-history causality，再测试 role reversal / repair，最后测试 transfer / retirement。

gaps.statement: 整合并验证现有 diagnostics，以区分 memory、task adaptation、semantic adaptation、alignment、mutual belief 与 interaction-history-dependent convention。
gaps.research_implication: 复用 partner-switch、positive-evidence、component-ablation 与 pseudo-dyad diagnostics；贡献应是 discriminant validation，而不是声称这些方法不存在。

gaps.statement: 把 informal / graphic paralanguage 与 multimodal structure 操作化地连接到 history-dependent adaptive embodied human–AI communication。
gaps.research_implication: 不能声称 theory absence；应在完成 A3/A4 与 D/F/G closest-work audit 后检验可证伪的 cross-layer mechanism。

gaps.statement: 当 multimodal signals 随 history 适应时，如何联合优化和评估 instrumental state/intent legibility 与 relational meaning。
gaps.research_implication: 研究重点是 trade-off 与 grounding；不能再声称 social 与 functional communication 从未被整合。

gaps.statement: 建立统一的 embodied human–agent causal protocol，结合 history severing、independent representation probes、reciprocity、repair、transfer 与 physical consequences。
gaps.research_implication: C5/C6 只能按一个 lineage 计数；先检验 shared-history causality，再分阶段测试 repair 与 transfer。

exam.title: Adaptive Multimodal Social Communication for Embodied AI: From Social Meaning and Shared Representations to Situated Adaptation
exam.core_question: 人类与具身智能体如何利用多模态、社会化和非正式表达建立共享意义，并随着互动历史、用户和情境变化形成自适应交流？
exam.written_target: 8–10 pages；正文使用约 25–30 篇，核心 corpus 30–35 篇，extended oral corpus 50–70 篇。

themes.name: Social and Multimodal Communication
themes.question: 多模态 signal 如何同时承载 information 与 social meaning？

themes.name: Representation and Pragmatics
themes.question: 为什么 communication 追求 contextually sufficient，而不是最大化 detail？

themes.name: Common Ground, Grounding, and Convention Formation
themes.question: 双方如何从 repeated interaction 形成 shared shorthand，并确认彼此理解？

themes.name: Embodied and Situated Robot Communication
themes.question: Robot 如何通过 motion、gaze、gesture、speech 与 visual signals 表达 intent、state、uncertainty 与 capability？

themes.name: Adaptation, Personalization, and Long-Term HRI
themes.question: Communication 如何随 user、relationship 与 interaction history 共同适应？

themes.name: Social, Cultural, and Relational Context
themes.question: Communicative priors 如何经由 interaction 被强化、修订或替换为 personal convention？

writing_plan.goal: 定义 embodied AI、multimodal social communication、informal visual language 与 adaptive communication，并提出总问题。
建立 communication = information + social meaning，避免 modality catalogue。
解释 pragmatics、common ground、abstraction、shared representation 与 convention。
连接 motion、gaze、gesture、visual signals、legibility 与 predefined semantics。
区分 behavior adaptation 与 communication co-development。
解释 social context、appropriation、relationship 与 cultural priors。
收束 emergent convention、adaptive visual communication、longitudinal grounding 与 social + instrumental meaning。

agent_readiness.warning: Source availability, Agent investigation, and researcher mastery are separate dimensions.

research_line.identity: 我研究人类与具身 AI Agent 如何通过 situated interaction，发展 adaptive、socially meaningful 的 multimodal communication。
research_line.core_question: How do socially meaningful multimodal signals become grounded, conventionalized, and adaptive in human–embodied AI interaction?

nodes.label: Meaning
nodes.question: Signal 表达什么 social / instrumental meaning？
nodes.detail: Informal visual expression、speech、gaze、gesture、motion 与 AR cue 不只是信息通道，也表达 stance、rapport、uncertainty 与 identity。

nodes.label: Grounding
nodes.question: 双方如何确认彼此理解？
nodes.detail: Pragmatic inference、joint attention、feedback 与 common ground 让 signal 在当前 context 中获得可接受解释。

nodes.label: Convention
nodes.question: Repeated interaction 如何生成 shared shorthand？
nodes.detail: 研究 conceptual pact、partner-specific convention、abstraction、repair、retention、forgetting 与 transfer。

nodes.label: Adaptation
nodes.question: Communication 如何随 user 与 history 改变？
nodes.detail: 区分 personalization、user modeling、mutual adaptation、co-adaptation 与真正共同生成的 convention。

nodes.label: Embodied Communication
nodes.question: WHAT / WHEN / WHERE / HOW 应如何进入 physical world？
nodes.detail: 把 motion、gaze、gesture、speech、visual display 与 spatial AR 作为可协调的 situated communication resources。

adjacent: Affective computing when it reveals mechanism
Multimodal foundation models as enabling infrastructure
out_of_scope: 只比较单一视觉效果是否更可爱
按国籍做静态 preference ranking
没有 meaning / grounding / adaptation 机制的 AI wrapper

next_questions.question: Do communication gains causally depend on shared dyadic history beyond same-producer exposure, style familiarity and task learning?
next_questions.design_stage: original dyad vs history-severed pseudo-dyad vs same-producer yoked vs shuffled, plus independent representation probes

next_questions.question: Can a grounded mapping survive role reversal and be repaired after controlled breakdown?
When should multimodal conventions transfer, retire or be renegotiated, and how do instrumental and relational meanings trade off?
next_questions.design_stage: partner/context transfer plus longitudinal post-novelty study
